evals.name: supply-requisition-queue
evals.prompt: Supply's requisition approval queue is way slower than usual and Halloran's complaining about it — can you figure out what's going on and put together a recommendation?
evals.expected_output: An investigation grounded in real repo sources (Halloran's interview, any relevant tickets/briefs) that reconciles his specific complaints against whatever structured evidence exists, forms a scoped recommendation, and is honest about what is and isn't confirmed by data versus only described qualitatively.
assertions: Report cites Halloran's interview directly (e.g. the 11-day vest-plate example) rather than describing the complaint secondhand
Report explicitly flags that no structured/quantitative requisition-timing data exists in this repo, so the finding rests on one qualitative account, not confirmed statistically
Recommendation stays scoped to Supply/requisitions and does not fold in or relitigate the unrelated Dispatch 4.2 routing investigation
References at least one specific file path from the repo as a cited source
States an explicit confidence level, or explicitly separates what's confirmed from what's still an open question

evals.name: console-ux-stakeholder-brief
evals.prompt: Our director wants to know what's going on with the handler console complaints (readability, dark mode, alerts) — put together a brief and something I can show her.
evals.expected_output: A stakeholder-ready brief grounded in the real interview transcripts, correctly scoped as console/UX debt separate from the 4.2 root-cause investigation, with a prototype or mockup to show, and a clear breakdown of what the director actually asked for versus the proposed answer.
assertions: Output separates 'what the director asked for' from 'the proposed answer' as distinct, identifiable sections or files, not blended into one
Cites at least two of the four interview sources (Ambrose, Aunt Dot, Halloran, Kip) with a direct quote about console UX
Names dark mode as Kip's specific, repeatedly-raised ask, not a generic UX item
Explicitly distinguishes this console-UX work from the 4.2 routing root-cause investigation, instead of conflating them as the same problem
Produces an actual prototype/mockup file (not just a text description of what one would look like)

evals.name: dispatch-acceptance-drop-cold
evals.prompt: Acceptance rate for Dispatch dropped after the August release and nobody can agree on why — can you dig in and tell me what's actually going on, and what we should do about it?
evals.expected_output: An investigation that reads the real CSV directly rather than trusting the pooled headline rate, discovers that a small number of responders collapsed toward zero offers while the rest absorbed more volume (the pooled-average artifact), reconciles this against tickets/interviews, and produces a confidence-scored recommendation plus something built to show for it.
assertions: Report computes real numbers directly from callout-history.csv (not just describing the drop qualitatively)

Identifies that a small subset of responders (not all 16) collapsed toward near-zero offers, and that the pooled/aggregate rate recovering is an artifact of that subset dropping out of the denominator
States an explicit numeric confidence score for its conclusion
Cross-checks at least one specific ticket claim against the real CSV data and states explicitly whether it's confirmed or contradicted
Produces a recommendation plus a built prototype/mockup, not analysis alone
